before_fields.text:
Where does Halloween come from? Follow the written record through Samhain, All Hallows' Eve, Burns's poem, and the customs that crossed the Atlantic.

This video uses synthetic narration and clearly labelled AI-generated historical reconstructions. Reconstructions are illustrative, not eyewitness records.

Chapters
00:00 The Story We Are Told
00:42 What the Medieval Texts Say
02:07 A God Who Never Was
02:40 All Hallows' Eve
03:40 A Night of Fortune-Telling
04:22 From Turnips to Pumpkins
05:26 Layers of a Night

Sources
- H-S01: Ronald Hutton, The Stations of the Sun (Oxford University Press, 1996)
- H-S02: Medieval Irish tales (Echtra Cormaic; Macgnímartha Finn) in scholarly translation
- H-S03: Coligny calendar, Lugdunum – Musée et théâtres romains, Lyon (LUG br.001) — https://lugdunum.grandlyon.com/fr/Oeuvre-incontournable/2381-Calendrier-gaulois-de-Coligny
- H-S04: Charles Vallancey, Collectanea de Rebus Hibernicis — https://wellcomecollection.org/works/ukgp57xu
- H-S05: Encyclopaedia Britannica, All Saints' Day — https://www.britannica.com/topic/All-Saints-Day
- H-S06: Robert Burns, Halloween (written 1785, Kilmarnock edition 1786)
- H-S07: Merriam-Webster, The History of 'Jack-O'-Lantern'; OED — https://www.merriam-webster.com/wordplay/the-history-of-jack-o-lantern
- H-S08: The Canadian Encyclopedia, Halloween — https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/halloween
- H-S09: Smithsonian Magazine, kale divination — https://www.smithsonianmag.com/arts-culture/the-halloween-tradition-best-left-dead-kale-as-matchmaker-100207686/

Images
- Robert Burns, engraving by William Nicholson, 1819. Library of Congress, LC-DIG-pga-07781. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2013645279/
- The witch, postcard, ca. 1900–1910. The New York Public Library, Image ID 1587780. https://digitalcollections.nypl.org/items/0d1887e0-c5c4-012f-e38e-58d385a7bc34
- Osservanza Master, All Saints in an Initial E or O, ca. 1430–40. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 1975.1.2484. Public Domain / CC0. https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/461011
- Spanish Painter, The Trinity Adored by All Saints, ca. 1400. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 39.54. Public Domain / CC0. https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/437743
- Greek Painter, All Saints, possibly 18th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 31.67.9. Public Domain / CC0. https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/436578
- Coligny calendar (detail), Lugdunum, Lyon. Photo: Ruthven, 2018, via Wikimedia Commons. CC0. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Calendriere_gaulois_de_Coligny_-_Mus%C3%A9e_gallo-romain_de_Fourvi%C3%A8re_(d%C3%A9tail).jpg
- Charles Vallancey, Collectanea de rebus hibernicis, Vol. II, title page, 1786. Wellcome Collection, EPB/B/54038.v2. Public Domain Mark. https://wellcomecollection.org/works/ukgp57xu
- Dorothea Lange, Halloween party at Shafter migrant camp, California, 1938. Library of Congress, LC-USF34-018556-D. https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2017770950/

NYPL describes the postcard as public domain under United States law and does not determine its status in other countries. Library of Congress records state no known restrictions. The 1938 California photograph is not the 1927 Canadian newspaper report. The Wellcome title page introduces the publication; it is not the page containing the claim.

English voice: Kokoro / Heart (af_heart), synthetic speech.
Japanese voice: VOICEVOX:冥鳴ひまり — https://www.meimeihimari.com/terms-of-use / https://voicevox.hiroshiba.jp/
Music: original ambient score by Quiet Origins.
